properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued July 24 at 3:03AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear NC out 20 nm...
Waters from Surf City NC to Little River Inlet SC from 20 to 60
NM...

At 302 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. These thunderstorms were
located along a line extending from 10 nm southeast of Ar355 to near
5 Mile Boxcars, moving southeast at 5 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until these storms pass. If caught on the
open water, prepare for deteriorating conditions. Make sure you and
your crew are wearing properly fitted life jackets.
properties.area: Coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear NC out 20 nm; Waters from Surf City NC to Little River Inlet SC from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued July 24 at 12:29AM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
At 1227 AM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 29 miles northeast of East Helena to 17 miles
west of White Sulphur Springs to 10 miles southeast of Toston to 6
miles southwest of Manhattan. Movement was east at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph.

SOURCE...Automated Sensors.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Townsend, White Sulphur Springs, Belgrade, Three Forks, Manhattan,
Toston, Fort Logan On The Smith River, Ringling, Fort Logan, Missouri
Headwaters State Park, Newlan Creek Reservoir, Logan, Maudlow,
Amsterdam, Trident, Church Hill, Menard, Madison Buffalo Jump State
Park, and Goose Bay.

Those attending the Red Ants Pants Festival are in the path of these
storms and should prepare for IMMINENT DANGEROUS WEATHER CONDITIONS.
properties.instruction:
Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Persons in campgrounds should consider seeking sturdy shelter until
these storms pass.
properties.area: Little Belt and Highwood Mountains; Big Belt, Bridger and Castle Mountains; Meagher County Valleys; Canyon Ferry Area; Missouri Headwaters; Gallatin Valley

FFWTOP

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Ottawa County in north central Kansas...

producing heavy rain in From near Ada to a few miles south of
Minneapolis. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.

drainage and low-lying areas.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 24 at 1:29AM EDT until July 24 at 10:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Rowan County in the Piedmont of North
Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1030 AM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 128 AM EDT, Automated river gauges indicated rapid rises due
to runoff from previous rainfall. Flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the warned area.
- Despite an earlier drop in river stage, continued runoff has
resulted in a recent increase in river stage along the Second
Creek watershed.  At 120 AM EDT, the stream gauge on Second Creek
near US-70 was in action stage, and rapidly approaching minor
flood stage, which for this stream gauge occurs at 14 feet.

Flooding of adjacent low-lying farmland is anticipated in
response, and should continue for much of the overnight. Impacted
crossings upstream may include at White Rd, Lyerly Rd, Upright
Rd, Graham Rd, Hall Rd, Childers Rd, and Bear Poplar Rd.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Piedmont Research Station.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 8:28AM AKDT until July 24 at 8:30AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Little Susitna River near Northern Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...Until 830 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways, mainly along and near North Sushana Drive.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 826 AM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly, especially
near the Little Susitna River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 22 at 9:00PM AKDT until July 24 at 3:15PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Willow Creek, Sheep Creek, Kashwitna River, Montana Creek
and their tributaries from the Parks Highway East between Willow
and the junction of the Talkeetna Spur Road.

* WHEN...Until 315 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 845 PM AKDT, river gauge and social media reports indicate
rises in water levels from heavy rain across the advisory
area. Minor flooding is expected, especially near Willow
Creek, Sheep Creek, Kashwitna River, Montana Creek and their
tributaries.
- For Willow Creek at Parks Highway:
At 8:26pm the stage was 9.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 10.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 11.0 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Thursday.

- For Willow Creek near Willow:
At 8:15pm the stage was 4.1 feet.
Flood Stage is 5.9 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 5.9 feet is expected around 10:00am
Thursday.
- Water levels on other rivers, creeks, or streams in the
advisory area, including Montana and Sheep Creeks and
Kashwitna River, may reach or exceed bankfull and remain
elevated through Thursday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
